title: Add attachment metadata index

context.summary: Persist searchable attachment metadata as derived state immediately after upload routing.
context.background: TASK-38 introduced document_media_metadata and document_metadata_index, but upload processing did not yet populate them or use them for search filters.

in: Extract base attachment metadata from RAW bytes during document.route without mutating the original object.
Persist size, MIME, extension, checksum, media type, container and available duration/dimension/page metadata to document_media_metadata.
Populate typed document_metadata_index rows for metadata filters.
Support structured metadata filters on document search for numeric and exact-value lookups.
Apply metadata filters to PostgreSQL full-text search and pgvector search paths.
Update integration tests, validators and documentation.
out: Full OCR, ASR, image captioning, face recognition or video keyframe processing.
Deep media probing through ffmpeg or heavyweight local model runtimes.
Changing the immutable RAW storage object.
Replacing the legacy chunks or chunk_vector_embeddings projections.

acceptance_criteria: document.route writes document_media_metadata for routed uploads.
document.route writes typed document_metadata_index entries for size, MIME, extension, checksum and media attributes.
Text, PDF, common image formats and WAV files get best-effort metadata from headers when available.
Document search accepts metadataFilters such as size_bytes <= 100MB and duration_ms between 10000 and 15000.
Metadata filters are enforced for artifact full-text search and pgvector search.
The RAW original storage object remains unchanged.

manual_checks: Confirm document search filters exclude documents outside metadata bounds.

risks: Header-only media parsing is intentionally best-effort; heavier media inspection belongs in later modality tasks.
Metadata filters are exact/range primitives for MVP and do not yet include a full query language.
definition_of_done: Task status is changed to accepted or done.
Branch is committed and merged back into master.
